summary: SRV DNS records resolving to stale port causes control-plane gRPC to connect to wrong service behind customer proxy
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent control-plane disconnects for their Private deployment. Symptoms show gRPC connections from control-plane components terminating with TLS handshake failures when attempting to open a stream to the artifact/model puller.

Impact:
- All model pulls intermittently fail for a subset (~20%) of control-plane requests originating from customer-managed subnet behind an egress inspection proxy.
- Resulting in degraded ability to fetch new model artifacts and occasional model-serving latencies and 503s from serving nodes.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC) connected to Redwood control-plane via VPCE in us-east-1.
- Customer uses an on-prem inspection proxy + egress forwarder (corporate proxy) that rewrites outgoing DNS and applies SRV record caching.

Observed behavior:
- SRV DNS responses returned to control-plane resolve to the legacy model-puller port (8443) for a small fraction of queries; current service expects 9443. gRPC attempts to connect to port 8443 and TLS handshake fails (server certificate is for 9443 endpoint).
- When SRV response returns correct port (9443), connections succeed.

Expected behavior:
- SRV responses should consistently map to the current control-plane port (9443). No TLS mismatch should occur.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) From customer subnet, query SRV record used by VPCE (e.g., _modelpull._tcp.control.redwood.example) multiple times in quick succession via the corporate proxy.
2) Observe a mix of responses with target:port fields 9443 and 8443.
3) Initiate a control-plane model pull gRPC connection to the returned host:port and observe TLS handshake failure when port=8443.
4) Repeat from a node bypassing corporate proxy (egress path) — all responses return 9443 and connections succeed.
logs:
Excerpt of client-side gRPC error (trimmed):
- time=2026-03-10T14:12:03Z caller=connector tls: first record does not look like a TLS handshake
- time=2026-03-10T14:12:03Z caller=connector dial target modelpull.us-east.redwood.example:8443 -> connection reset
DNS query log (pcap):
- 14:11:59.123 SRV _modelpull._tcp.control.redwood.example -> target=artpull-1.internal.redwood.example, port=8443
- 14:12:00.045 SRV _modelpull._tcp.control.redwood.example -> target=artpull-2.internal.redwood.example, port=9443
- 14:12:01.873 SRV _modelpull._tcp.control.redwood.example -> target=artpull-1.internal.redwood.example, port=8443
investigation:
Initial triage by Support: confirmed TLS mismatch originates from control-plane dialing port 8443. Customer egress proxy has an SRV caching layer that retains old responses beyond TTL due to cache keying on hostname only (ignores service/port).
SRE notes: Redwood pivoted model-puller to 9443 in Feb 2026 (see internal rollout notes). Some customer proxies have pinned SRV mappings or aggressive caching and will continue to return 8443 until cache invalidation.
Hypothesis: Corporate proxy rewrites/serves cached SRV records (old port) for ~20% of lookups because it shard-caches between multiple upstream resolvers; one upstream still authoritative for legacy port.
Data gathered:
- Packet captures from customer confirm mixed SRV answers.
- VPCE logs show control-plane healthchecks succeed when connections use 9443.

2026-03-10 18:05 - SRE (Luca Romero): Reproduced mixed SRV responses from customer's resolver (via their forwarded resolver). Opened reachout to Proxy vendor — they confirmed default behavior can cache SRV with stale port mapping if upstream responses vary across resolvers.

2026-03-11 09:45 - Support (Maya Chen): Workaround suggestion provided — add explicit SRV cache flush for that service or configure proxy to respect SRV TTL and disable port-coalescing cache. Customer testing now.

2026-03-11 11:10 - Customer (Rajiv Singh): Applied cache flush and set SRV cache strategy to 'per-service' instead of 'host-only'. Observed immediate drop in 8443 responses. Reports model pulls restored.
Marked as 'Waiting on Support' for verification steps to be persisted in runbook.

2026-03-12 08:15 - SRE (Luca Romero): Confirmed customer metrics show 99.9% success after workaround. Planning follow-up: add explicit validation to our agent to prefer target port from SRV and retry on TLS mismatch with canonical port 9443 before failing — discussed with platform team (see PR).
resolution:
Workaround: Customer disabled SRV cache coalescing and flushed SRV cache on their proxy. This removed stale 8443 answers and restored normal control-plane connectivity.
Permanent/future mitigation: Engineering to add a conservative SRV-aware retry: if TLS handshake fails on SRV-provided port, agent will retry on the canonical/current port (9443) once before surfacing failure. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5910.
Follow-ups:
- Support runbook updated with SRV-cache troubleshooting steps.
- Reach out to Proxy vendors to document SRV caching caveats for Private deployments.
- Customer to perform a formal SRV cache policy review during next maintenance window.
